standard_prerequisites.name: Additive functors commute with direct sums
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the implication from additivity to the preservation of binary direct sums in either direction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Addition of morphisms through the diagonal and the codiagonal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the description of f + g as the composite A -> A + A -> B + B -> B via the diagonal and the codiagonal
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the sum of two morphisms to which the functor is applied in the final step of the proof.

core_obligations: (1) implies (2) and (3) (proof lines 1701-1703): an additive functor commutes with direct sums by the cited lemma, so both comparison maps are isomorphisms.

(2) implies zero object and zero morphisms (proof lines 1704-1715): with 0 the zero object of the source, the comparison F(0) + F(0) -> F(0 + 0) = F(0) being an isomorphism forces the diagonal map on Hom(F(0), C) to be bijective for every C, so F(0) is a zero object of the target and F carries zero morphisms to zero morphisms; the same argument starts from (3).

(2) and (3) are equivalent (proof lines 1715-1724): the composite F(A) + F(B) -> F(A + B) -> F(A) + F(B) is given by the displayed matrix with F(1) on the diagonal and F(0) off it, hence is the identity, so the two comparison maps are mutually inverse.

(2) and (3) imply (1) (proof lines 1725-1749): writing f + g as the composite through the diagonal and the codiagonal, the author applies F and checks that the resulting diagram commutes, the middle square by functoriality together with the vanishing of zero morphisms and the two triangles by the isomorphisms of (2) and (3); going around the bottom computes F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g).
proof_roadmap: Derive preservation of direct sums from additivity.
Get the zero object and zero morphisms from either comparison map.
Show the two comparison maps are mutually inverse using the matrix of F(1) and F(0).
Recompute F applied to the description of f + g as a composite.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes additive functors between additive categories as those for which either comparison map between F(A) + F(B) and F(A + B) is an isomorphism (statement lines 1686-1698). The proof is a complete argument: the forward implication is the companion statement on additive functors and direct sums (proof lines 1701-1703); the diagonal argument recovers the zero object and the vanishing of zero morphisms (proof lines 1704-1715); the two comparison maps are shown to be mutually inverse by computing their composite as the identity matrix (proof lines 1715-1724); and additivity is recovered by applying the functor to the description of a sum of two morphisms and checking the resulting diagram (proof lines 1725-1749). The non-formal content is the last diagram check. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
